column3: “at the edge of” renders “on the border of.”
“Iyim” is the short form of Iye-abarim (verse 44).
“figured stones” renders “maskiyyot,” carved images, and “molten images” renders “images of molten metal.”
“according to your families” renders “by your clans”; “the larger” and “the smaller” render “the many” and “the few.”
NASB reverses the pair: the Hebrew has “thorns (sikkim) in your eyes and pricks (tsninim) in your sides”; “trouble you” renders “oppose you.”
